subject: Clarifying backup purge timelines, deletion workflow, and log retention
messages:
From: Alice Porter <security@fintechco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on retention / backups / subprocessors

Hi Naomi,

Following up on our DPA review — a few focused questions from our compliance team so we can close the security gate: 

1) Data deletion: when a customer requests account deletion or dataset deletion, what is Redwood's end-to-end workflow? Specifically: what systems are deleted/zeroed, how are caches/embeddings handled, and how long until content is unrecoverable?

2) Backups and snapshots: what backup cadence and retention do you maintain? What are the hard purge timelines for backups after a deletion request?

3) Logs & audit trails: are there exceptions to deletion for logs or audit records? If so, what fields are retained and for how long?

4) Subprocessors & transfers: which subprocessors store backups or logs, and are any backups replicated cross-border? We need visibility for our DPA annex.

Can you send the retention matrix and any evidence (DPA clauses, SOC2 artifact pointers) that specifies these timelines?

Thanks — if easier we can hop on a 20-min call, but docs first would be great.

Best,
Alice Porter
Senior Security Manager
FinTechCo

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Porter <security@fintechco.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on retention / backups / subprocessors

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary; I attached our retention matrix (redwood-dpa-retention-matrix.pdf) and a short FAQ. Happy to follow up with legal if you need DPA language.

1) Deletion workflow (customer-initiated):
- Customer requests deletion via Console API or Support ticket. Request is acknowledged by automation and routed to a deletion job.
- Primary data (model inputs/outputs) are deleted from live stores within 24 hours; delete operations issue tombstones across services.
- KV caches and prefix caches are purged asynchronously; we mark keys for immediate eviction and run eviction within 48 hours.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: most are stored in vector stores that receive the same delete markers; those shards are compacted during weekly maintenance.
- Final irrecoverability: for live stores, data is unrecoverable within 7 days; for backups/snapshots see (2).

2) Backups & snapshots (purge timeline):
- Daily hot backups retained for 30 days (rolling).
- Weekly cold snapshots retained for 90 days to support disaster recovery and cross-region failover.
- Immutable DR snapshots (used for full-cluster restore) are retained for up to 180 days in exceptional cases with documented justification.
- Purge mechanics: when a deletion is requested, we mark the object and flag associated backup entries. Purge jobs run weekly; typical completion window for removing data from all backup layers is 30–45 days depending on snapshot retention and replication state.
- Note: the 30–45 day window accounts for immutable snapshot rotation; we can discuss contract-level reductions where feasible but there are operational constraints.

3) Logs & audit trails (exceptions):
- Audit logs that record system-level events are retained for 13 months by default for incident investigations and compliance.
- We attempt to minimize PII in logs; where identifiers are required for debugging we retain hashed account IDs and redact user-generated content.
- We can offer scoped log access / limited retention windows for specific customers on request; however, some security logs (e.g., authentication and billing events) are preserved longer for fraud detection and legal obligations.

4) Subprocessors & transfers:
- Subprocessors involved in backups/long-term storage: CloudStorageCo (US), ArchiveEU Ltd (EU region replication), LogStore Inc.
- Cross-border replication: snapshots may be replicated to an EU region for customers with EU footprints; transfers rely on SCCs + our DPA.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-retention-matrix.pdf (retention by artifact), short FAQ.

If you need a DPA addendum (shorter backup purge window or custom log-retention rules) we can prepare a draft. From an operational standpoint a 30-day max for all backups is possible in many cases but requires an exception/approval and will change our DR posture (we'd document the risk).

Let me know the specific asks (e.g., "purge all backups within 30 days and reduce log retention to 90 days") and I will loop in Privacy & Legal and produce a draft amendment.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alice Porter <security@fintechco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on retention / backups / subprocessors

Hi Naomi — thanks, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups so we can formalize: 

- Does the 30–45 day backup purge window guarantee removal of all customer-derived embeddings and cached model prompts (some of those are stored in blob backups)? We need explicit statement whether derived artifacts are included.

- For logs: can you provide a scoped list of the log classes that will never be truncated below 12 months (we have a regulator requirement around transaction logs)?

- We'd like to propose a DPA addendum to require a 30-day maximum for all backups and a 90-day maximum for application logs. Is your team able to accept that as a contract term (we can do this as an exception with a signature)? If so, please send a DocuSign-ready addendum and an internal escalation path for any operational incidents triggered by the shorter retention.

Also, please confirm whether any of the subprocessors you listed keep independent backups of customer content beyond Redwood's control (we specifically need to know for ArchiveEU Ltd).

Thanks — if you can get a draft addendum and an estimated time to have this signed, that will speed our procurement.

Regards,
Alice

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Porter <security@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on retention / backups / subprocessors

Alice — looping in Rishi (Ops) and Monica (Legal) to action. Summary and next steps below + attached draft addendum.

Short answers:
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, cached prompts) are covered by the same deletion markers and included in backup purge workflows; confirmed they are included. Removal completion is dependent on snapshot churn but our target is 30 days for hot/cold (we currently publish 30–45).
- Non-truncated log classes (default): security/authentication events, billing/usage events, and system integrity/audit logs — retained 13 months. We can scope a narrower set for FinTechCo but need signoff from Legal due to fraud/investigation requirements.
- Subprocessors: ArchiveEU Ltd maintains replicated snapshots for EU failover but does not keep independent long-term customer backups beyond Redwood's replication window; we will request a written attestation from ArchiveEU and share it.

Action items:
1) Monica to review & finalize the attached DPA_addendum_fintechco_draft.docx (proposed: 30-day backup purge, 90-day application log retention, carveouts for security logs).
2) Rishi to confirm operational timeline and escalate if DR posture changes. Internal ticket: RED-4536 (ops: backup purge SLA request).
3) Naomi to provide DocuSign link once Legal signs off and to provide escalation path (pager/team contact) for incidents triggered by reduced retention.

Attachments: DPA_addendum_fintechco_draft.docx (proposal), retention matrix (already attached earlier). HubSpot deal: HS-8821.

Estimated timeline: Legal review + ops confirmation ~ 3 business days; DocuSign thereafter assuming no substantial edits.

--

naomi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
